subject: frontend-engineering
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Philosophy, The Ref / State Decision, Ref Callbacks, forwardRef / ref-as-prop, useImperativeHandle, Ref Forwarding in Compound Components, Refs and the Client/Server Boundary, Common Anti-Patterns, Verification) and the React docs cited under Grounding Sources.

cases.scenario: A developer stores the current text-input values in a useRef 'to avoid re-renders on every keystroke,' then reads ref.current during render to show a live character count. The count never updates.
cases.context: It is a controlled-feeling form where the count must reflect the latest input.
cases.question: How should the agent fix this?
expected_flags: The value drives what is rendered (the live count) — it is STATE, so use useState
Reading ref.current during render returns stale data because refs do not trigger renders
Frames the choice as semantic (inside vs outside the render cycle), not a performance optimization
The 'avoid re-renders' perf concern was a phantom for almost all forms
expected_fix_hints: Replace useRef with useState for the input value
Derive the character count from the state value in render
absent_signals: Do not keep the value in a ref and read it during render
Do not add a forceUpdate hack to make the ref-stored value re-render

cases.scenario: A polling component stores its setInterval id in useState and clears it on unmount. It re-renders on a cadence even when no displayed data changed.
cases.context: The interval id is never shown in the UI; only the fetched data is.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the re-render storm?
expected_flags: The interval id is not rendered — it is a mutable instance value, so store it in useRef, not useState
useState for the id causes a pointless re-render every time it is set
Clean up the interval in the same effect (clearInterval in the cleanup)
Distinguishes the displayed data (state) from the side-effect handle (ref)
expected_fix_hints: Move the interval id to a useRef
Keep only the fetched data in state
absent_signals: Do not keep the interval id in state

cases.scenario: An author builds a compound Tabs component. A consumer does <Tabs.Trigger ref={triggerRef}> and tries to focus it on mount, but triggerRef.current is null. The intermediate wrapper renders a styled <button> but drops the ref.
cases.context: The library is meant to support focus management and third-party DOM integration.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the primitive?
expected_flags: Every layer between consumer and the underlying DOM element must forward the ref through to the <button>
Use the Radix Slot / composeRefs pattern to merge the consumer ref with the library's internal ref
On React 19 accept ref as a prop and pass it down; on React 18 use forwardRef
A compound-component primitive that does not forward refs is not finished
expected_fix_hints: Forward ref={composeRefs(forwardedRef, internalRef)} onto the rendered <button>
Ensure each wrapping primitive accepts and passes the ref
absent_signals: Do not leave the wrapper dropping the ref
Do not tell the consumer to query the DOM directly as a workaround

cases.scenario: A Modal exposes its entire internal API (open, close, isOpen getter, setTitle, getChildrenCount, internalState) to the parent via useImperativeHandle. The parent reads isOpen through the handle and its UI does not stay in sync.
cases.context: The parent mostly needs to open and close the modal; it occasionally needs to reflect open state in its own render.
cases.question: How should the agent redesign the handle?
expected_flags: Expose the minimum surface — only what the parent needs (open/close), not the whole internal API
Do not expose state-read functions; reading isOpen via a method makes the parent's render unreactive to it
If the parent must reflect open state, lift state up (isOpen prop + onOpenChange callback)
Default to props/callbacks; reserve the imperative handle for genuine escape-hatch needs
expected_fix_hints: Trim the handle to { open, close }
Lift isOpen into a controlled isOpen prop with onOpenChange
absent_signals: Do not expose the full internal API surface
Do not read state through an imperative getter

cases.scenario: A Server Component creates a ref with useRef and passes it to a Client Component child to measure it. The build errors / the ref is never populated.
cases.context: The page is a React Server Components app using the App Router and 'use client' boundaries.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the boundary issue?
expected_flags: Refs only work in Client Components — no useRef in a Server Component, and refs are not serializable across the 'use client' boundary
Server Components produce HTML on the server; there is no DOM node or client runtime to hold the mutable container
Move the part of the tree that needs the ref into a Client Component marked 'use client'
Notes the broader boundary mechanics belong to client-server-boundary
expected_fix_hints: Mark the measuring wrapper 'use client' and create the ref there
Keep the ref usage entirely in client-only space
absent_signals: Do not try to pass a ref as a prop from a Server Component
Do not return a ref from a Server Action

cases.context: The team treats anything involving useRef, useState, or hooks as 'the ref-patterns person's job.'
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?

Dependency-array discipline, Rules of Hooks, and custom-hook conventions belong to hooks-patterns
Offer the in-scope part: the ref-vs-state decision for individual mutable values and the ref family mechanics
Redirects rather than answering out of lane

Provide the ref-or-state call for the specific mutable values in the form

cases.scenario: A team on React 18 wants to 'modernize' by replacing all forwardRef wrappers with the React 19 ref-as-prop syntax across the codebase in one PR.
cases.context: The app is pinned to React 18 and will not upgrade for another quarter.
cases.question: How should the agent advise?
expected_flags: Ref-as-prop is a React 19 feature — applying it on React 18 breaks (function components cannot accept a ref prop directly there)
Keep forwardRef while on React 18; migrate to ref-as-prop when React 19 is the active version
forwardRef still works on React 19 for backward compatibility; codemods exist to migrate when the time comes
Sequences the migration to the actual React version, not the desire to modernize
expected_fix_hints: Defer the ref-as-prop migration until React 19 ships in the app
Use the official codemod at upgrade time
absent_signals: Do not replace forwardRef with ref-as-prop on a React 18 codebase
Do not modernize syntax ahead of the runtime that supports it
